Yes. The clearest match is work that treats GNNs as fast surrogates for semidefinite programs: one paper studies when GNNs can recover optimal linear SDP solutions, showing standard GNNs fail but a more expressive architecture can emulate first-order solver updates and provide strong predictions that can warm-start SDP solving for practical speedups [1]. Another paper gives a Max-Cut-specific GNN proxy for SDP relaxations inside branch-and-bound, predicting primal- and dual-feasible SDP solutions and substantially reducing bounding cost compared with an SDP solver [2].

They differ in scope: [1] is a general study of expressive power for linear SDPs plus warm-starting on synthetic and SdpLib benchmarks, while [2] is a specialized, feasibility-preserving proxy for Max-Cut SDP relaxations in exact optimization, trained self-supervised and designed to plug directly into branch-and-bound [1,2].
